title: Evidence you can check
subtitle: Understand the results, challenge the claim and see what proof comes next
audience: Curious readers, decision makers and reviewers

pages.title: What the evidence lets you say

blocks.text: **The public repository supports an executed local continuity exercise.** Its software reconstructs specified obligations, tries a permitted route and checks the resulting artifacts against the retained promise. That is a useful, inspectable engineering result. Its meaning depends on the exact exercise and the evidence behind it. [R1, R2, R3]

blocks.caption: Each broader claim needs additional observations. The public main-branch evidence reaches executed local software; customer delivery and a repeatable commercial service require their own proof. [R2, R4, R6]

pages.title: One order book makes the idea concrete
pages.kicker: An executed software example with synthetic orders

blocks.text: A restored application can run while its order book is wrong. The base exercise exposes that problem with three label orders. The retained event history contains an amendment and a cancellation that the stale restore has missed. [R2]

blocks.text: The authoritative total is **1,900 units in two orders**. Correct reconciliation must restore B, use A’s amended quantity and keep C canceled. A route cannot improve its apparent result by quietly removing an obligation. [R2, R3]

Both obligations completed: 1,900/1,900.

Both obligations completed: 1,900/1,900.

blocks.label: Two verdicts can both be correct
blocks.text: In the constrained run, the tested capacity constraint is respected and the full promise fails. Refusing an order prevents overbooking; the unfulfilled 800 units remain visible. A passing test assertion can correctly report that partial outcome. [R2, R3]

These counts refer to durable local software outputs. The exercise does not establish printed labels or delivery to real customers. Physical production and customer acceptance need their own observations. [R2, R3]

pages.title: What “independent” means here
pages.kicker: Separate checking against the same promise

blocks.text: Here, the useful separation is concrete: **the verifier reconstructs the obligations through its own source replay and checks current durable outputs against a separately retained contract and reference**. A candidate’s assertion that it succeeded is not sufficient acceptance evidence. [R2, R4]

blocks.name: verification_loop
blocks.caption: Construct, challenge and check against the original promise. A repair is tested again; the verdict stays scoped to the evidence actually examined. [R2, R3, R4]

items: Retain the original authority outside the candidate’s permitted control; changing a candidate-side copy must not change the obligation.
Read current artifacts when checking again. A saved Passport describes a past assessment.
Challenge the verifier itself, including false acceptance and false rejection. A checker that refuses every result is not qualified.

blocks.label: The trust boundary remains explicit
blocks.text: The host, controller, services, authored journal, clock and verifier remain trusted. Separate code paths under shared project authorship are not third-party certification. Matching hashes establish byte identity, not authentic or complete real customer instructions. [R3, R4]

pages.title: Give a critic a decisive test
pages.kicker: How an attractive claim can be disproved

blocks.text: A useful objection identifies an observation that would change the verdict. The documented challenge families below make that practical. They are a reading and review guide to retained experiments, not new experiments performed for this book. [R2, R3]

rows: Change a candidate’s 1,900-unit obligation to 1,850 while retaining the original authority.
The changed package cannot satisfy the original full promise. Coherent candidate-side hashes do not make the rewrite authoritative.
Alter an output while keeping an old favorable Passport.
Fresh verification must assess the changed artifact. The old report cannot certify its present state.
Remove the independently retained reference pin.
Authority remains NOT ESTABLISHED. Recomputing a convenient replacement pin does not close the gap.
Make the backup share the failed dependency.
An unavailable logical backup cannot support completed fulfillment through that route.
Present a valid positive control to a deliberately defective checker.
False rejection must also disqualify a checker. Successful evidence should be accepted when the stated conditions are met.
Give a competent conventional method the same tools and information.
A tie does not establish improvement. Any advantage claim must survive the complete comparison and its cost boundary.

blocks.text: For a reproducible challenge, preserve the original authority, identify the altered copy or test mutation, record the target’s answer, then retain the separate reference verdict. State precisely which claim fails. The project’s shared-helper counterexample—accepting 1,850 against an original 1,900—shows why checking the checker matters. [R3, R9]

blocks.label: Read the right verdict
blocks.text: An adversarial test can pass because it exposed false acceptance. In that same record, the defective checker’s qualification fails. Test success and business success answer different questions. [R2, R3]

pages.title: Reproduce the pinned software record
pages.kicker: Commands for the public main-branch revision

blocks.text: Use Linux x86_64 with seccomp BPF, Python 3.10 or later, and Node.js for the repository-wide website tests. The default exercise uses local synthetic data and standard-library components. Choose unused output paths; previous attempts are preserved. These commands were not executed for this editorial collection. [R2, R5]

git clone https://github.com/MontrealAI/CONTINUITY.git
cd CONTINUITY
git checkout --detach \
  396227d8da2f55f674f479de16089c7ce28ef290
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
python3 -m continuity_harness --language en demo \
  --out /tmp/continuity-evidence-demo-001
python3 -m continuity_harness --language en verify-suite \
  --in-dir /tmp/continuity-evidence-demo-001
python3 -m continuity_harness --language en compare \
  --out /tmp/continuity-evidence-comparison-001
python3 -m continuity_harness --language en verify-suite \
  --in-dir /tmp/continuity-evidence-comparison-001
python3 -m continuity_harness --language en challenge \
  --out /tmp/continuity-evidence-challenges-001

Read the structured result and each obligation. Suite exit 0 means the expected assertions passed; it can include an expected partial outcome. Individual verification of a partial promise returns 3. Exit 2 indicates a command error. Historical qualification uses its own code and archive pins in R3. [R2, R3]

blocks.label: One distinction that prevents a false recheck
blocks.text: In this v0.1 interface, verify-suite applies to indexed demo/comparison outputs, not challenge directories. For an individual challenge, use its exact verify command, authority path and original reference digest. Keep that pin independently of candidate-controlled data. [R2]

pages.title: The next decisive proof
pages.kicker: One actual promise, one controlled commercial test

blocks.text: The next useful observation is an authorized rehearsal for one real business, with an actual provider and a capable alternative. The repository’s printer pilot is a proposal without real approvals. Its value is the falsifiable test it defines. [R6]

rows: Was the promise met?
An authentic order, frozen acceptance terms and an authorized assessor’s decision about the output actually produced. Distinguish a rehearsal substitute from physical customer delivery.
Was the arrangement feasible?
Real participant consent; lawful data use; qualified capacity net of other commitments; usable dependencies; funded production, correction and remaining obligations.
Was this commercially worthwhile?
The buyer’s actual purchase decision, collected payment, complete campaign costs and residual liabilities, compared with the same-promise conventional alternative and no purchase.

blocks.text: Count preparation, failed attempts, integration, staff time, reservations, execution, verification, transport where relevant, financing, support and refunds. Record when funds are needed and when they clear. A positive modeled margin cannot establish these observations. [R6, R7]

blocks.label: The claim should grow with the evidence
blocks.text: One paid, accepted pilot supports a claim about that transaction. A repeatable service needs further evidence about continued demand, available capacity and complete economics. A useful retained method needs a separate fresh task and a fair comparison before it earns a successor-benefit claim. [R6]

A conventional winner, a no-buy decision or a failed exercise is still a decisive finding. Preserve the conditions and the reason. The next experiment can address the demonstrated obstacle rather than assume the market already exists. [R6, R8]

pages.title: Leave an evidence package another person can use
pages.kicker: From a report to an inspectable record

blocks.text: A reader should be able to locate the original promise, the execution, the current check and the claim being made. The Harness separates these records so a later review can inspect the result again. [R2]

rows: INDEX.json
The run list, completeness and retained reference pins. Preserve its custody when transferring the evidence.
Retained authority
The contract, source history and original reference. Identify which facts are authored and which have external authentication.
Durable evidence and controller record
The actual database, artifacts, observed transitions, interruptions and timing within the declared trust model.
RESULT.json and bilingual Passports
The assessed outcome, failed or missing conditions and exact verification command. A saved presentation is a record of its assessment.
Fresh verification receipt
Which revision, current files and retained reference were checked, what the verdict was, and when the check occurred.
